source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: More context: I am specifically targeted folks looking for estate planning services (as opposed to other estate law services like estate administration, probate, elder law, etc). Got kind of confused when I saw this forecast suggest that I'd see a sharp drop off in ROAS when spending $2,000 or more. Felt weird that I could only squeeze out 20 monthly form fills (and maybe 3 conversions) when targeting a pretty large geographic area (all of New Jersey, and the affluent Philly suburb counties). But maybe that's the limit? Maybe the forecast tool isn't accurate pre-campaign launch? Once, you'd have a chance to look let me know what is even possible to know at this point.

assessment_objectives: Assess whether the forecasted decline in return on ad spend at monthly spending of $2,000 or more is plausible.
Assess whether approximately 20 monthly form fills and possibly 3 conversions represent a realistic limit.
Assess the reliability of the forecast before campaign launch.
Explain what campaign feasibility can be determined from the available pre-launch information.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Hey Stephen - looks good. One question before we start. Definitely fine with starting at $2k per month to test the water. But do you see room for scaling? I know we will have a better idea once we have some data from the few months. But just curious about what you can see now.

value_updates.scaling_assessment: Assess the room to scale beyond the initial monthly budget using currently available information before several months of campaign performance data exist.

routing_warnings.description: The broad completion claim explicitly identifies the audit and buildout proposal but does not establish that the campaign scaling assessment was completed.
The client authorizes the seven-hour campaign buildout rather than changing or resolving the scaling assessment.
